metadata.note: The Penn Yan and New York Railway -- seven miles from Penn Yan down the Keuka Lake Outlet to Dresden on Seneca Lake, laid in the bed of a dead canal. The Crooked Lake Canal, built 1830-1833, had climbed the same outlet with 28 locks against a 270-foot drop in under eight miles, and never earned its keep; the state abandoned it in 1877, the year the railroad was incorporated. Penn Yan businessmen had the right of way by 1884 and the first train ran Aug 3 1884. Its Penn Yan terminus was the steamboat dock where the outlet leaves Keuka Lake, handing passengers to the lake boats; its other end met the Fall Brook line just south of Dresden station. Consolidated into the Syracuse, Geneva and Corning Railway on Oct 1 1885, leased to the New York Central and Hudson River in 1899 and merged into the New York Central in 1914, it ran out its days as the NYC Penn Yan Branch, losing passengers in 1953 and freight by about 1970. Hurricane Agnes ended it in 1972 and the corridor reopened as the Keuka Outlet Trail on Jul 4 1984 -- the third transport use of the same seven miles.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syracuse,_Geneva_and_Corning_Railway (the SG&C established 1875, opened Dec 10 1877, leased to and operated by the Fall Brook Coal Company for 20 years from 1881; consolidated without a change of name with the Penn Yan and New York Railroad Company on Oct 1 1885, citing Poor's Manual of the Railroads of the United States vol. 22, 1889; leased to the New York Central and Hudson River Railroad in 1899; merged with the Geneva, Corning and Southern Railroad in 1909 and into the New York Central Railroad in 1914; its locale is given as Corning to Geneva plus the Dresden Branch, Penn Yan to Dresden)

metadata.not_yet_sourced: No timetable has been consulted for any era, so every headway here is an estimate, as are the running speeds. The 1877 incorporation is documented but the company's construction dates are not, only the Aug 3 1884 first train. 1953 is given as the year passenger service was dropped, without a dated last train. The freight end date is bracketed rather than known: the branch is absent from the May 1 1970 Penn Central timetable and Hurricane Agnes is blamed in 1972, but no abandonment filing has been checked, and the feature is drawn only to 1953 because that is when passengers stopped. Naming is muddled in the sources -- 'Penn Yan and New York Railway' and 'Penn Yan and New York Railroad Company' are both used, and at least one secondary account has the 1885 consolidation being between those two rather than with the Syracuse, Geneva and Corning; the Wikipedia article on the SG&C, citing Poor's Manual, is followed here. The short stretch from the mapped east end into Dresden village and the junction with the Fall Brook line is not drawn.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.

segments.note: Incorporated 1877, the year the state abandoned the Crooked Lake Canal, and built in the canal's own bed along the Keuka Lake Outlet. By 1884 a group of Penn Yan businessmen had bought the right of way, and the first train ran Aug 3 1884. The Penn Yan end was at the steamboat dock on the south bank of the outlet where it leaves Keuka Lake, so rail met the lake steamers; the Dresden end joined the Fall Brook line just south of Dresden station. Frequency estimated/unsourced

properties.geometry_source: Digitized right-of-way from Wikimedia Commons (Data:Syracuse, Geneva and Corning Railway.map, CC BY 4.0), the feature titled 'Penn Yan and New York Railway', 217 points, Penn Yan to Dresden. Measures 11.22 km / 6.97 mi. Independently checked against OpenStreetMap (ODbL): the ways carrying the Keuka Lake Outlet Trail and the ones still tagged 'Penn Yan Branch' with railway=abandoned were stitched by shortest path from the Penn Yan trailhead to the Dresden end, giving 6.96 mi between identical endpoints. Both agree with the 6.7 miles quoted for the modern Keuka Outlet Trail. The mapped corridor stops about 0.6 km short of Dresden village, where the branch met the Fall Brook line.
properties.geometry_quality: Real-traced throughout from the Commons digitization, 217 points, no approximated legs. Traced 6.97 mi against 6.43 mi given for the Dresden Branch in the Fall Brook corporate figures and 6.7 mi for the modern Keuka Outlet Trail; the traced line runs to the outlet mouth at Penn Yan, which likely accounts for the difference. Independently reproduced from OpenStreetMap at 6.96 mi between identical endpoints.

segments.note: Worked thereafter as the New York Central's Penn Yan Branch. Passenger service was dropped in 1953; the last passenger train to serve Penn Yan at all was the Pennsylvania Railroad's No. 596 on the north-south Elmira and Sodus branch, on Jan 2 1956. Freight lasted into the Penn Central years -- the line is already absent from Penn Central Employee Timetable No. 4 of May 1 1970 -- and Hurricane Agnes finished the corridor in 1972. The right of way reopened as the Keuka Outlet Trail on Jul 4 1984. Frequency estimated/unsourced
